title: finish-hook fence/race scratchpad
content:
Summary:
This is a scratchpad tracking a recurring failure during node bootstrap in staging-rackB. New hosts intermittently go NotReady for ~30-90s and sometimes never recover. Problem windows correlate with the provisioning helm chart's post-install hook (finish-node.sh) which performs ephemeral unmounts, netns cleanup, and a custom fence-tool detach.

Observed symptoms:
- Node flips to NotReady shortly after kubelet startup then often recovers.
- Some nodes end up with kubelet crashloop or unable to find /var/lib/containerd/ overlayfs snapshots.
- kube-proxy and CNI agents frequently CrashLoopBackOff during the window.
- dmesg shows nvme controller reset/failure on some hosts.

Hypothesis (working):
- Ordering/race between cloud-init/systemd units, kubelet startup, and helm post-install hook leads to the hook removing or detaching resources that kubelet and containerd are still using.
- finish-node.sh sometimes times out (exit 124) which leaves partial state (lazy unmounts scheduled, deferred detach).
- Device detach or namespace file removal leads to missing mountpoints or cgroup dirs -> kubelet reports "no such file or directory" for cgroups, snapshots, mounts.
- The fence-tool deferred detach on NVMe may trigger kernel-level device reset that disrupts containerd and overlayfs.

What I ran (commands + key excerpts):
- systemctl show -p After cloud-init.target kubelet.service
  -> kubelet has Wants=multi-user.target, After=containerd.service cloud-init.target

- journalctl -u kubelet -b -o short-precise | sed -n '1,200p'
  -> "failed to list snapshots: error opening /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots: no such file or directory"
  -> "failed to write kubelet-config: write /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml: no space left on device" (on node with small ephemeral disk)

- tail -50 /var/log/cloud-init-output.log
  -> "/opt/provisioner/hooks/finish-node.sh: line 84: fence-tool: command timed out (exit 124)"
  -> "Unmounting /mnt/tmp_disk: target is busy; lazy unmount scheduled"

- ls -la /var/lib/kubelet (during NotReady)
  -> directory empty or missing plugins directory on affected hosts

- kubectl describe node <node>
  -> Conditions: KubeletNotReady, message: "failed to get cgroups for pods: open /sys/fs/cgroup...: no such file or directory"

- dmesg | grep -i nvme | tail -n 40
  -> "nvme nvme0: failed to reset controller"
  -> "device-mapper: reload ioctl failed: Device or resource busy"

- ip netns list (after hook)
  -> namespace file from provisioner missing on some nodes

Debug traces / snippets saved locally:
- finish-node.sh (relevant sections):
  "# try to unmount ephemeral, then remove netns file
   umount /mnt/tmp_disk || umount -l /mnt/tmp_disk
   rm -f /var/run/netns/provisioner-$PROVISION_ID || true
   fence-tool --force --detach $DEV || (echo 'deferred' && exit 124)"

- kubelet journal (around same timestamp):
  "E failed to ensure mount for volume \"...\": operation not permitted
   E failed to start containerd runtime: failed to list snapshots"

Pattern analysis:
- Nodes with slower disk or containerd cold start more likely to fail (timing-sensitive).
- Nodes where finish-node.sh finished successfully (exit 0) usually recover quickly.
- finish-node.sh exit 124 appears on majority of failing nodes.
- Some failures coincide with kernel nvme resets which correlate with fence-tool detach attempts.

Immediate mitigation ideas tried (quick results):
- Increase helm hook timeout (prelim patch in PR 274) -> reduced frequency but not eliminated (race still possible).
- Add extra systemd ordering: make finish-node.sh run Before=kubelet.service? Tried and observed kubelet then starts after hook but cloud-init ordering complicated; risk of delaying kubelet too long on other fleets.
- Convert fence-tool detach to softer unmount-only step -> reduced nvme resets but leftover device references caused containerd to complain about "device busy".

Next investigative steps (todo):
- Reproduce deterministically in a lab node with verbose tracing: add sleep in kubelet.service ExecStartPre to widen race window and capture what finish-node.sh does.
- Add strace to fence-tool to see what syscalls lead to kernel resets.
- Capture kernel oops/tracepoints around nvme reset time (echo 1 > /sys/module/nvme/parameters/debug?).
- Snapshot timing: instrument finish-node.sh to log timestamps for each step and write to /var/log/provisioner-hook.log.
- Check containerd startup logs earlier (systemd unit StartLimit?) and overlayfs directories before/after hook.
- Evaluate switching to node annotation & later controller-based cleanup instead of in-hook device detach.

Proposed long-term fix ideas:
- Make hooks idempotent and safe when concurrent with kubelet: avoid removing dirs that kubelet owns, use lockfiles, or check for processes using mountpoints (lsof/fuser) and skip detach if busy.
- Prefer marking node as "provisioning-complete" via API and run heavy cleanup asynchronously after node reports Ready.
- Avoid hard detach of NVMe in hook; perform graceful fencing from central service which can coordinate with kubelet and containerd via CRI shim or node agent.

Quick checklist for remediation runbook:
- [ ] Instrument finish-node.sh with detailed logs and timestamps
- [ ] Increase hook timeout temporarily in staging and monitor failure rate
- [ ] Patch fence-tool to attempt graceful detach or return non-fatal status if busy
- [ ] Add gating in hook: if /var/lib/kubelet exists and has content, skip destructive steps
- [ ] Run controlled repro with sleep injected into kubelet ExecStartPre

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does containerd create overlayfs snapshot directories before kubelet starts or after? Need to confirm lifecycle ordering.
- Could systemd cgroup v2 configuration affect path expectations (/sys/fs/cgroup...) leading to the "no such file"?
- Why do only a subset of nodes trigger NVMe controller resets? Hardware variance or specific kernel+firmware combos?

Notes for handoff to infra-provisioner owners (Marco):
- Hook logs show exit 124 and lazy unmount usage; prefer non-blocking cleanup + non-priv drop when running as hook.
- Consider moving fence-tool detach out of helm hook into post-provision controller to reduce host-time contention.

If stuck, escalate to SRE for kernel trace and to storage team for NVMe detach behavior.

Log attachments (local):
- /var/log/provisioner-hook.log.* (rotated snapshots)
- /var/log/kubelet-hook-debug-2025-09-02.txt
- collected dmesg snippets under /tmp/node-debug-<id>/

Last tried quick patch (result):
- PR #274 increased helm hook timeout to 10m and added simple "if [ -d /var/lib/kubelet ] && [ $(ls -A /var/lib/kubelet | wc -l) -gt 0 ]; then echo 'kubelet active, skip heavy cleanup'; exit 0; fi".
- Outcome: failure rate dropped from ~12% to ~3% in staging runs but still seen on slower nodes.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep this as a living scratchpad; paste kernel traces and fence-tool strace here when available.
- If we shift cleanup to controller, document state machine for provisioning -> ready -> cleanup and ensure idempotency.

-- Evelyn
